# KPI Catalog

<!-- Generated by `python -m app.analytics.kpis.catalog` from app/analytics/kpis/definitions.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

20 registered KPIs. Each is computed by `calculate_kpi(db, key, params)` from a registered, parameterised SQL template plus a documented value rule. See [analytics.md](analytics.md) for conventions (periods, point-in-time rule, filters, result contract).

| # | Key | Name | Unit | Formula |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `revenue` | Revenue | SGD | SUM(daily_revenue.revenue) over dates in [start, end] |
| 2 | `mrr` | Monthly Recurring Revenue | SGD per month | SUM(subscriptions.monthly_recurring_revenue) for records in force at the close of end_date |
| 3 | `arr` | Annual Recurring Revenue | SGD per year | MRR x 12 |
| 4 | `revenue_growth` | Revenue Growth | ratio | (current period revenue - comparison period revenue) / comparison period revenue |
| 5 | `logo_churn_rate` | Churn Rate - Logo | ratio | churned opening customers / customers active at the close of (start - 1 day) |
| 6 | `revenue_churn_rate` | Churn Rate - Revenue | ratio | MRR of churned opening customers (at churn) / MRR in force at the close of (start - 1 day) |
| 7 | `retention_rate` | Retention Rate | ratio | 1 - logo churn rate (same opening base) |
| 8 | `nrr` | Net Revenue Retention | ratio | (opening MRR - churned MRR - contraction MRR + expansion MRR) / opening MRR |
| 9 | `cac` | Customer Acquisition Cost | SGD per customer | SUM(marketing_campaigns.spend) / SUM(marketing_campaigns.conversions) for campaign-weeks in the period |
| 10 | `clv` | Customer Lifetime Value | SGD per customer | (closing MRR / closing customers) / (churned customers / opening customers / months in period) |
| 11 | `arpu` | Average Revenue Per User (Account) | SGD per customer per month | MRR / active customers (both at the close of end_date) |
| 12 | `average_order_value` | Average Order Value | SGD (annual contract value) | SUM(deal_value of Won opportunities) / COUNT(Won opportunities), close_date in the period |
| 13 | `conversion_rate` | Conversion Rate | ratio | SUM(marketing_campaigns.conversions) / SUM(marketing_campaigns.leads) for campaign-weeks in the period |
| 14 | `pipeline_value` | Pipeline Value | SGD (annual contract value) | SUM(deal_value) where created_date <= end_date and (close_date IS NULL or close_date > end_date) |
| 15 | `win_rate` | Win Rate | ratio | COUNT(Won) / COUNT(Won or Lost), close_date in the period |
| 16 | `sales_cycle` | Sales Cycle | days | SUM(close_date - created_date) / COUNT(closed), Won and Lost, close_date in the period |
| 17 | `support_ticket_volume` | Support Ticket Volume | tickets | COUNT(support_tickets) with created_at in the period |
| 18 | `average_resolution_time` | Average Resolution Time | hours | SUM(resolution_time of Resolved tickets) / COUNT(Resolved tickets), created_at in the period |
| 19 | `product_adoption` | Product Adoption | ratio | AVG(product_features.adoption_rate) over days in the period (adoption_rate = feature daily active users / platform daily active users) |
| 20 | `customer_count` | Customer Count | customers | COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) of subscription records in force at the close of end_date |

## Definitions

### `revenue`: Revenue

**Definition.** Recognised revenue (subscription plus usage) for all days in the period.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | SUM(daily_revenue.revenue) over dates in [start, end] |
| Value rule | `value = revenue` |
| Unit | SGD |
| Time grain | Flow over any period (day, month, quarter, year, custom range). |
| Interpretation | Total revenue recognised in the period; compare with the prior period via revenue_growth. |
| Dependencies | `daily_revenue`, `customers` |
| SQL template | `revenue` (components: revenue, subscription_revenue, usage_revenue, observations) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan`, `revenue_type` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan`, `revenue_type`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result is reported as no_data |

**Limitations**

- Includes subscription and usage (API overage) revenue; filter revenue_type to isolate one stream.
- Subscription revenue is recognised as MRR / days-in-month per day in force, so a full calendar month recognises exactly the MRR; partial months are prorated.
- If the period extends beyond the data coverage, only observed days are included.

### `mrr`: Monthly Recurring Revenue

**Definition.** Contracted monthly recurring revenue of all subscriptions in force at the close of the period's end date.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | SUM(subscriptions.monthly_recurring_revenue) for records in force at the close of end_date |
| Value rule | `value = mrr` |
| Unit | SGD per month |
| Time grain | Point in time: the state at the period end (e.g. MRR for 2026-Q2 = MRR at 30 June 2026). |
| Interpretation | Recurring run-rate at the end of the period; excludes one-off and usage revenue. |
| Dependencies | `subscriptions`, `customers` |
| SQL template | `recurring_state` (components: mrr, active_customers) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan` |
| Empty result | an empty result is reported as no_data |

**Limitations**

- Point-in-time metric: movements inside the period are not visible (see the MRR bridge).
- Excludes usage (overage) revenue.
- Customers acquired before the data window carry a single opening record, so MRR history before 2024-09-01 is not available.

### `arr`: Annual Recurring Revenue

**Definition.** Annualised recurring run-rate at the period end.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | MRR x 12 |
| Value rule | `value = mrr x 12` |
| Unit | SGD per year |
| Time grain | Point in time (period end). |
| Interpretation | Annualised equivalent of MRR; a run-rate, not contracted annual value. |
| Dependencies | `mrr` |
| SQL template | `recurring_state` (components: mrr, active_customers) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan` |
| Empty result | an empty result is reported as no_data |

**Limitations**

- Inherits MRR limitations; assumes the current MRR persists for 12 months.

### `revenue_growth`: Revenue Growth

**Definition.** Relative change in recognised revenue between the period and a comparison period.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | (current period revenue - comparison period revenue) / comparison period revenue |
| Value rule | `value = current_revenue / comparison_revenue - 1` |
| Unit | ratio |
| Time grain | Two flows; the comparison defaults to the immediately preceding period of the same shape. |
| Interpretation | Positive = growth, negative = decline (e.g. -0.01 = a 1% decline). |
| Dependencies | `revenue` |
| SQL template | `revenue_comparison` (components: current_revenue, comparison_revenue, current_observations, comparison_observations) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan`, `revenue_type` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan`, `revenue_type` |
| Empty result | an empty result is reported as no_data |
| Comparison period | required (defaults to the preceding period of the same shape) |

**Limitations**

- Both periods must lie fully within the data coverage.
- Usage revenue and partial periods scale with day counts; full-month subscription revenue does not.

### `logo_churn_rate`: Churn Rate - Logo

**Definition.** Share of customers active at the period opening whose last day of service falls in the period.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | churned opening customers / customers active at the close of (start - 1 day) |
| Value rule | `value = churned_customers / opening_customers` |
| Unit | ratio |
| Time grain | Over the requested period (not annualised: a quarterly rate is roughly 3x a monthly rate). |
| Interpretation | Higher = more accounts lost. Compare like-for-like periods. |
| Dependencies | `subscriptions`, `customers` |
| SQL template | `opening_cohort` (components: opening_customers, churned_customers, opening_mrr, churned_mrr, expansion_mrr, contraction_mrr) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Customers acquired during the period are excluded from numerator and denominator.
- Churn date = last day of service (subscriptions.end_date of the churned record).
- A plan filter uses the plan in force at the period opening.

### `revenue_churn_rate`: Churn Rate - Revenue

**Definition.** Share of opening MRR lost because opening customers churned during the period.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | MRR of churned opening customers (at churn) / MRR in force at the close of (start - 1 day) |
| Value rule | `value = churned_mrr / opening_mrr` |
| Unit | ratio |
| Time grain | Over the requested period (not annualised). |
| Interpretation | Revenue-weighted churn; large accounts churning raise it more than logo churn. |
| Dependencies | `subscriptions`, `customers` |
| SQL template | `opening_cohort` (components: opening_customers, churned_customers, opening_mrr, churned_mrr, expansion_mrr, contraction_mrr) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Excludes contraction (downgrades); NRR captures contraction.
- Churned MRR is the MRR at the time of churn, which may differ from opening MRR if the customer expanded or contracted before churning.

### `retention_rate`: Retention Rate

**Definition.** Share of customers active at the period opening who had not churned by the period end.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | 1 - logo churn rate (same opening base) |
| Value rule | `value = 1 - churned_customers / opening_customers` |
| Unit | ratio |
| Time grain | Over the requested period. |
| Interpretation | Logo retention; complements logo churn exactly. |
| Dependencies | `logo_churn_rate` |
| SQL template | `opening_cohort` (components: opening_customers, churned_customers, opening_mrr, churned_mrr, expansion_mrr, contraction_mrr) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Inherits logo churn limitations.

### `nrr`: Net Revenue Retention

**Definition.** Recurring revenue kept from the opening customer base, including their expansion, contraction and churn, relative to their opening MRR.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | (opening MRR - churned MRR - contraction MRR + expansion MRR) / opening MRR |
| Value rule | `value = (opening_mrr - churned_mrr - contraction_mrr + expansion_mrr) / opening_mrr` |
| Unit | ratio |
| Time grain | Over the requested period; annual NRR uses a 12-month period (e.g. trailing_12_months). |
| Interpretation | Above 1.0 = the existing base grew net of losses; below 1.0 = net shrinkage. |
| Dependencies | `subscriptions`, `customers` |
| SQL template | `opening_cohort` (components: opening_customers, churned_customers, opening_mrr, churned_mrr, expansion_mrr, contraction_mrr) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- New-business MRR and all movements of customers acquired during the period are excluded by design.
- Usage (overage) revenue is excluded.

### `cac`: Customer Acquisition Cost

**Definition.** Marketing programme spend per customer acquired by marketing campaigns.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | SUM(marketing_campaigns.spend) / SUM(marketing_campaigns.conversions) for campaign-weeks in the period |
| Value rule | `value = spend / conversions` |
| Unit | SGD per customer |
| Time grain | Flow; weekly campaign rows belong to the period containing their Monday. |
| Interpretation | Cost to acquire one marketing-sourced customer; lower is more efficient. |
| Dependencies | `marketing_campaigns` |
| SQL template | `marketing_funnel` (components: spend, impressions, clicks, leads, conversions, observations) |
| Filters | `acquisition_channel`, `campaign` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `acquisition_channel`, `campaign`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result is reported as no_data |
| Not reported at grain | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `plan`, `customer_id` (returns insufficient_data with the reason) |

**Limitations**

- Only marketing programme spend is recorded; sales salaries, commissions and tooling are not in the dataset, so this understates fully loaded CAC.
- Covers marketing-sourced customers only; Outbound Sales and Referral acquisitions have no recorded spend.
- Conversions are counted in the week they occur, not linked to the week the lead was generated.

### `clv`: Customer Lifetime Value

**Definition.** Revenue-based lifetime value: recurring revenue per customer multiplied by the expected customer lifetime implied by the period's logo churn.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | (closing MRR / closing customers) / (churned customers / opening customers / months in period) |
| Value rule | `value = (closing_mrr / closing_customers) / (churned_customers / opening_customers / period_months)` |
| Unit | SGD per customer |
| Time grain | Uses the requested period for churn and its end for ARPA; use >= 12 months for stability. |
| Interpretation | Approximate recurring revenue a typical customer generates over their lifetime. |
| Dependencies | `arpu`, `logo_churn_rate` |
| SQL template | `customer_lifetime_value` (components: opening_customers, churned_customers, closing_mrr, closing_customers, period_months) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Revenue-based: the dataset contains no gross-margin assumption, so CLV is not margin-adjusted and overstates profit-based CLV.
- Assumes a constant monthly churn rate (geometric lifetime = 1 / monthly churn).
- Ignores expansion, contraction and usage revenue; short periods make it volatile.

### `arpu`: Average Revenue Per User (Account)

**Definition.** Recurring revenue per active customer account at the period end (ARPA).

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | MRR / active customers (both at the close of end_date) |
| Value rule | `value = mrr / active_customers` |
| Unit | SGD per customer per month |
| Time grain | Point in time (period end). |
| Interpretation | Average monthly recurring revenue per account; the 'user' is the customer account. |
| Dependencies | `mrr`, `customer_count` |
| SQL template | `recurring_state` (components: mrr, active_customers) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan` |
| Empty result | an empty result is reported as no_data |

**Limitations**

- Excludes usage revenue.
- Accounts, not individual seats or end users.

### `average_order_value`: Average Order Value

**Definition.** Average annual contract value of opportunities won in the period.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | SUM(deal_value of Won opportunities) / COUNT(Won opportunities), close_date in the period |
| Value rule | `value = won_value / won_opportunities` |
| Unit | SGD (annual contract value) |
| Time grain | Flow over close dates. |
| Interpretation | Typical deal size; segment mix strongly influences it. |
| Dependencies | `sales_opportunities` |
| SQL template | `closed_opportunities` (components: closed_opportunities, won_opportunities, lost_opportunities, won_value, lost_value, total_cycle_days) |
| Filters | `segment`, `region`, `sales_rep`, `opportunity_type`, `customer_id` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `segment`, `region`, `sales_rep`, `opportunity_type`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Includes New Business and Expansion deals unless filtered by opportunity_type.
- deal_value is annual contract value (12 x MRR added), not the first invoice.

### `conversion_rate`: Conversion Rate

**Definition.** Marketing lead-to-customer conversion: customers converted per marketing-qualified lead.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | SUM(marketing_campaigns.conversions) / SUM(marketing_campaigns.leads) for campaign-weeks in the period |
| Value rule | `value = conversions / leads` |
| Unit | ratio |
| Time grain | Flow; same-period ratio of weekly campaign rows. |
| Interpretation | Share of marketing leads that became paying customers. |
| Dependencies | `marketing_campaigns` |
| SQL template | `marketing_funnel` (components: spend, impressions, clicks, leads, conversions, observations) |
| Filters | `acquisition_channel`, `campaign` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `acquisition_channel`, `campaign`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result is reported as no_data |
| Not reported at grain | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `plan`, `customer_id` (returns insufficient_data with the reason) |

**Limitations**

- Numerator and denominator are counted in the same weeks; it is not a lead-cohort conversion.
- Covers the marketing funnel only; sales-opportunity conversion is reported by win_rate and sales analytics.

### `pipeline_value`: Pipeline Value

**Definition.** Total annual contract value of opportunities open at the close of the period end date.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | SUM(deal_value) where created_date <= end_date and (close_date IS NULL or close_date > end_date) |
| Value rule | `value = pipeline_value` |
| Unit | SGD (annual contract value) |
| Time grain | Point in time (period end). |
| Interpretation | Unweighted value of deals still in progress. |
| Dependencies | `sales_opportunities` |
| SQL template | `open_pipeline` (components: open_opportunities, pipeline_value) |
| Filters | `segment`, `region`, `sales_rep`, `opportunity_type`, `customer_id` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `segment`, `region`, `sales_rep`, `opportunity_type` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Unweighted: stage probabilities are only known for the current (as-of) pipeline; see sales analytics.
- Historical pipeline is reconstructed from created/close dates; the stage at that time is not recorded.

### `win_rate`: Win Rate

**Definition.** Share of opportunities closed in the period that were won.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | COUNT(Won) / COUNT(Won or Lost), close_date in the period |
| Value rule | `value = won_opportunities / closed_opportunities` |
| Unit | ratio |
| Time grain | Flow over close dates. |
| Interpretation | Higher = a larger share of closed deals won. Compare segments separately. |
| Dependencies | `sales_opportunities` |
| SQL template | `closed_opportunities` (components: closed_opportunities, won_opportunities, lost_opportunities, won_value, lost_value, total_cycle_days) |
| Filters | `segment`, `region`, `sales_rep`, `opportunity_type`, `customer_id` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `segment`, `region`, `sales_rep`, `opportunity_type`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Every CRM record is an opportunity, including deals lost at the Lead stage.
- Open opportunities are excluded until they close.

### `sales_cycle`: Sales Cycle

**Definition.** Average days from opportunity creation to close for opportunities closed in the period.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | SUM(close_date - created_date) / COUNT(closed), Won and Lost, close_date in the period |
| Value rule | `value = total_cycle_days / closed_opportunities` |
| Unit | days |
| Time grain | Flow over close dates. |
| Interpretation | Average elapsed time to a decision; Enterprise deals take longer. |
| Dependencies | `sales_opportunities` |
| SQL template | `closed_opportunities` (components: closed_opportunities, won_opportunities, lost_opportunities, won_value, lost_value, total_cycle_days) |
| Filters | `segment`, `region`, `sales_rep`, `opportunity_type`, `customer_id` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `segment`, `region`, `sales_rep`, `opportunity_type`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Includes won and lost deals; open opportunities are excluded.
- The mean is sensitive to long deals; sales analytics also reports the median for won deals.

### `support_ticket_volume`: Support Ticket Volume

**Definition.** Number of support tickets created in the period.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | COUNT(support_tickets) with created_at in the period |
| Value rule | `value = tickets` |
| Unit | tickets |
| Time grain | Flow over ticket creation dates. |
| Interpretation | Support demand; normalise by active customers when comparing periods. |
| Dependencies | `support_tickets`, `customers` |
| SQL template | `support_tickets` (components: tickets, resolved_tickets, unresolved_tickets, total_resolution_hours) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `ticket_category`, `ticket_priority` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `ticket_category`, `ticket_priority`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Volume is not normalised for customer growth; see tickets per active customer.

### `average_resolution_time`: Average Resolution Time

**Definition.** Mean hours from creation to resolution for tickets created in the period and resolved.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | SUM(resolution_time of Resolved tickets) / COUNT(Resolved tickets), created_at in the period |
| Value rule | `value = total_resolution_hours / resolved_tickets` |
| Unit | hours |
| Time grain | Flow over ticket creation dates. |
| Interpretation | Higher = slower support. |
| Dependencies | `support_tickets`, `customers` |
| SQL template | `support_tickets` (components: tickets, resolved_tickets, unresolved_tickets, total_resolution_hours) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `ticket_category`, `ticket_priority` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `ticket_category`, `ticket_priority`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Unresolved tickets are excluded from the denominator (reported as unresolved_tickets); recent periods are biased towards faster tickets because slow ones may still be open.
- The mean is skewed by long tickets; support analytics also reports the median.

### `product_adoption`: Product Adoption

**Definition.** Average daily share of platform daily active users who used the feature.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | AVG(product_features.adoption_rate) over days in the period (adoption_rate = feature daily active users / platform daily active users) |
| Value rule | `value = average_daily_adoption_rate` |
| Unit | ratio |
| Time grain | Flow over days; one value per feature. |
| Interpretation | Feature penetration among active users. |
| Dependencies | `product_features` |
| SQL template | `product_features` (components: average_daily_adoption_rate, average_daily_feature_users, observed_feature_days, first_observed_date) |
| Filters | `product_feature` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `product_feature`, `month`, `quarter` |
| Empty result | an empty result is reported as no_data |
| Required | one of product_feature as filter or dimension |
| Not reported at grain | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `plan`, `customer_id` (returns insufficient_data with the reason) |

**Limitations**

- The denominator is all platform daily active users; plan eligibility is not recorded, so no eligible-user denominator is available.
- Platform-level only: no segment, region or customer breakdown.
- A feature has no rows before its launch date.

### `customer_count`: Customer Count

**Definition.** Distinct customers with a subscription in force at the close of the period end date.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Formula | COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) of subscription records in force at the close of end_date |
| Value rule | `value = active_customers` |
| Unit | customers |
| Time grain | Point in time (period end). |
| Interpretation | Active paying accounts; see customer analytics for opening, new and churned counts. |
| Dependencies | `subscriptions`, `customers` |
| SQL template | `recurring_state` (components: mrr, active_customers) |
| Filters | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `customer_id`, `plan` |
| Breakdown dimensions | `region`, `country`, `segment`, `industry`, `acquisition_channel`, `plan` |
| Empty result | an empty result means zero counts (counts report 0; ratios report insufficient_data) |

**Limitations**

- Point in time: customers who joined and left within the period are not counted.

## SQL templates

### `revenue`

Recognised revenue (subscription + usage) for days in the period. Temporal semantics: `flow`. Components: revenue, subscription_revenue, usage_revenue, observations.

```sql
SELECT
    {dimension} AS dimension_value,
    SUM(r.revenue) AS revenue,
    COALESCE(SUM(r.revenue) FILTER (WHERE r.revenue_type = 'subscription'), 0) AS subscription_revenue,
    COALESCE(SUM(r.revenue) FILTER (WHERE r.revenue_type = 'usage'), 0) AS usage_revenue,
    COUNT(*) AS observations
FROM daily_revenue AS r
JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
WHERE r.date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date{filters}
GROUP BY 1
```

### `revenue_comparison`

Recognised revenue in the current and the comparison period, side by side. Temporal semantics: `flow`. Components: current_revenue, comparison_revenue, current_observations, comparison_observations.

```sql
SELECT
    {dimension} AS dimension_value,
    COALESCE(SUM(r.revenue) FILTER (WHERE r.date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date), 0) AS current_revenue,
    COALESCE(SUM(r.revenue) FILTER (
        WHERE r.date BETWEEN $comparison_start_date AND $comparison_end_date), 0) AS comparison_revenue,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date) AS current_observations,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.date BETWEEN $comparison_start_date AND $comparison_end_date) AS comparison_observations
FROM daily_revenue AS r
JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = r.customer_id
WHERE (r.date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date
       OR r.date BETWEEN $comparison_start_date AND $comparison_end_date){filters}
GROUP BY 1
```

### `recurring_state`

Subscriptions in force at the close of the period's end date. Temporal semantics: `point_in_time`. Components: mrr, active_customers.

```sql
SELECT
    {dimension} AS dimension_value,
    SUM(s.monthly_recurring_revenue) AS mrr,
    COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id) AS active_customers
FROM subscriptions AS s
JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE s.start_date <= $end_date AND (s.end_date IS NULL OR s.end_date > $end_date OR (s.end_date = $end_date AND s.status = 'superseded')){filters}
GROUP BY 1
```

### `opening_cohort`

Customers active at the period opening and what happened to them during the period. Temporal semantics: `cohort_flow`. Components: opening_customers, churned_customers, opening_mrr, churned_mrr, expansion_mrr, contraction_mrr.

```sql
WITH customer_lifetimes AS (
    SELECT cu.*, ch.churn_date
    FROM customers AS cu
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT customer_id, end_date AS churn_date FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'churned'
    ) AS ch ON ch.customer_id = cu.customer_id
),
opening AS (
    SELECT s.customer_id, s.plan, s.monthly_recurring_revenue AS opening_mrr
    FROM subscriptions AS s
    WHERE s.start_date <= $opening_date AND (s.end_date IS NULL OR s.end_date > $opening_date OR (s.end_date = $opening_date AND s.status = 'superseded'))
),
cohort AS (
    SELECT {dimension} AS dimension_value, o.customer_id, o.opening_mrr
    FROM opening AS o
    JOIN customer_lifetimes AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE TRUE{filters}
),
movements AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        SUM(monthly_recurring_revenue - previous_mrr) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'expansion') AS expansion_mrr,
        SUM(previous_mrr - monthly_recurring_revenue) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'contraction') AS contraction_mrr
    FROM subscriptions
    WHERE change_type IN ('expansion', 'contraction') AND start_date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
churned AS (
    SELECT customer_id, monthly_recurring_revenue AS churned_mrr
    FROM subscriptions
    WHERE status = 'churned' AND end_date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date
)
SELECT
    cohort.dimension_value,
    COUNT(*) AS opening_customers,
    COUNT(churned.customer_id) AS churned_customers,
    SUM(cohort.opening_mrr) AS opening_mrr,
    COALESCE(SUM(churned.churned_mrr), 0) AS churned_mrr,
    COALESCE(SUM(movements.expansion_mrr), 0) AS expansion_mrr,
    COALESCE(SUM(movements.contraction_mrr), 0) AS contraction_mrr
FROM cohort
LEFT JOIN churned ON churned.customer_id = cohort.customer_id
LEFT JOIN movements ON movements.customer_id = cohort.customer_id
GROUP BY 1
```

### `customer_lifetime_value`

Closing recurring revenue per customer and the period's logo churn among opening customers. Temporal semantics: `cohort_flow`. Components: opening_customers, churned_customers, closing_mrr, closing_customers, period_months.

```sql
WITH customer_lifetimes AS (
    SELECT cu.*, ch.churn_date
    FROM customers AS cu
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT customer_id, end_date AS churn_date FROM subscriptions WHERE status = 'churned'
    ) AS ch ON ch.customer_id = cu.customer_id
),
flow AS (
    SELECT
        {dimension} AS dimension_value,
        COUNT(*) AS opening_customers,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE c.churn_date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date) AS churned_customers
    FROM subscriptions AS s
    JOIN customer_lifetimes AS c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_date <= $opening_date AND (s.end_date IS NULL OR s.end_date > $opening_date OR (s.end_date = $opening_date AND s.status = 'superseded')){filters}
    GROUP BY 1
),
closing AS (
    SELECT
        {dimension} AS dimension_value,
        SUM(s.monthly_recurring_revenue) AS closing_mrr,
        COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id) AS closing_customers
    FROM subscriptions AS s
    JOIN customer_lifetimes AS c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
    WHERE s.start_date <= $end_date AND (s.end_date IS NULL OR s.end_date > $end_date OR (s.end_date = $end_date AND s.status = 'superseded')){filters}
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    flow.dimension_value,
    flow.opening_customers,
    flow.churned_customers,
    closing.closing_mrr,
    closing.closing_customers,
    CAST($period_months AS DOUBLE) AS period_months
FROM flow
LEFT JOIN closing ON closing.dimension_value = flow.dimension_value
```

### `marketing_funnel`

Campaign spend and funnel volumes for campaign-weeks starting in the period. Temporal semantics: `flow`. Components: spend, impressions, clicks, leads, conversions, observations.

```sql
SELECT
    {dimension} AS dimension_value,
    SUM(m.spend) AS spend,
    SUM(m.impressions) AS impressions,
    SUM(m.clicks) AS clicks,
    SUM(m.leads) AS leads,
    SUM(m.conversions) AS conversions,
    COUNT(*) AS observations
FROM marketing_campaigns AS m
WHERE m.date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date{filters}
GROUP BY 1
```

### `closed_opportunities`

Opportunities closed (won or lost) with a close date in the period. Temporal semantics: `flow`. Components: closed_opportunities, won_opportunities, lost_opportunities, won_value, lost_value, total_cycle_days.

```sql
SELECT
    {dimension} AS dimension_value,
    COUNT(*) AS closed_opportunities,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'Won') AS won_opportunities,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'Lost') AS lost_opportunities,
    COALESCE(SUM(o.deal_value) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'Won'), 0) AS won_value,
    COALESCE(SUM(o.deal_value) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'Lost'), 0) AS lost_value,
    SUM(datediff('day', o.created_date, o.close_date)) AS total_cycle_days
FROM sales_opportunities AS o
WHERE o.stage IN ('Won', 'Lost') AND o.close_date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date{filters}
GROUP BY 1
```

### `open_pipeline`

Opportunities open at the close of the period's end date (created, not yet closed). Temporal semantics: `point_in_time`. Components: open_opportunities, pipeline_value.

```sql
SELECT
    {dimension} AS dimension_value,
    COUNT(*) AS open_opportunities,
    COALESCE(SUM(o.deal_value), 0) AS pipeline_value
FROM sales_opportunities AS o
WHERE o.created_date <= $end_date AND (o.close_date IS NULL OR o.close_date > $end_date){filters}
GROUP BY 1
```

### `support_tickets`

Tickets created in the period, with their resolution status as of the dataset end. Temporal semantics: `flow`. Components: tickets, resolved_tickets, unresolved_tickets, total_resolution_hours.

```sql
SELECT
    {dimension} AS dimension_value,
    COUNT(*) AS tickets,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.status = 'Resolved') AS resolved_tickets,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.status = 'Open') AS unresolved_tickets,
    SUM(t.resolution_time) FILTER (WHERE t.status = 'Resolved') AS total_resolution_hours
FROM support_tickets AS t
JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
WHERE t.created_at >= $start_date AND t.created_at < $end_date + INTERVAL 1 DAY{filters}
GROUP BY 1
```

### `product_features`

Daily feature adoption rows (feature DAU / platform DAU) for days in the period. Temporal semantics: `flow`. Components: average_daily_adoption_rate, average_daily_feature_users, observed_feature_days, first_observed_date.

```sql
SELECT
    {dimension} AS dimension_value,
    AVG(p.adoption_rate) AS average_daily_adoption_rate,
    AVG(p.active_users) AS average_daily_feature_users,
    COUNT(*) AS observed_feature_days,
    strftime(MIN(p.date), '%Y-%m-%d') AS first_observed_date
FROM product_features AS p
WHERE p.date BETWEEN $start_date AND $end_date{filters}
GROUP BY 1
```
